content.text: I need a Glypherie logo. Can you generate few variants?
I’ll use the imagegen skill to create a few distinct Glypherie logo directions, using the project’s visual context to guide them.

I’m exploring three directions: an outline-based **G**, a pixel-grid **G**, and an editorial wordmark. I’ll use Glypherie’s existing charcoal, orange, and green palette, with simple shapes and generous spacing informed by [established identity guidance](https://indeed.design/brand/typography/). These will be concepts for comparison.
The three directions are generated, but the transparent output introduced halos around some edges. I’m making clean white-background versions so the letterforms are easier to compare.

Generated three concepts:

1. **Outline** — orange G with Bézier-inspired nodes; my pick for Glypherie.
2. **Raster** — green pixel G, emphasizing bitmap generation.
3. **Foundry** — expressive serif lettering with an orange accent.

Saved the PNGs and [full prompts](/Users/dimitri/Documents/Code/personal/Inkplate/font_generator/out/diagnostics/glypherie-logo-concepts/2026-10-26/prompts.json) in [the concepts folder](/Users/dimitri/Documents/Code/personal/Inkplate/font_generator/out/diagnostics/glypherie-logo-concepts/2026-10-26), using built-in image generation. These are raster concepts for selection and refinement.
